# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):

I am Blind. I can feel the bomb but cannot see colors or read the manual. My action set is limited to cutting wires at positions 1, 2, or 3. The current state shows `[?]` for everything, meaning I don't know if there are even three wires, or what their properties are. However, the Action Board explicitly lists `WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]`, which strongly implies there are exactly three wires present and accessible to me.

The Deaf monkey can see the bomb (colors/markings).
The Mute monkey can read the manual (rules/instructions).

I need information from both to act safely.
First, I should establish contact with the Deaf monkey to confirm the physical layout and any visual cues on the wires themselves (like labels or specific colors that might correspond to rules). Since I can gesture, I will use gestures to ask the Deaf monkey for information about the wires. A common convention in these puzzles is to ask "What do you see?" or specifically about the wires.

Let's try to get a baseline description from the Deaf monkey. I'll gesture towards the wire area and then make a questioning or descriptive gesture. Since I don't have a shared language yet, I'll start by indicating the wires and asking for a count or status. But wait, the Deaf monkey sees *everything*. Maybe I should just signal "Help" or "Wait".

Actually, the most critical missing piece is the rule set. The Mute monkey has the manual. I can speak to the Mute monkey. I should ask the Mute monkey for the rules regarding the wires. Specifically, how to determine which wire to cut.

To the Mute: I will speak. I need to know the condition for cutting a wire.
To the Deaf: I will gesture. I need to know the color of the wires, as colors often trigger conditions in the manual.

Let's formulate the messages.
For Mute (Speech): "What are the rules for the wires? When is it safe to cut one?"
For Deaf (Gesture): I need to convey "Colors of wires?". I'll point to the wire section (👇) and then hold up three fingers (✌️ + ☝️ = 3? No, ✌️ is 2, ☝️ is 1. 🤟 is 6? No. Let's stick to simple symbols). 👆 (point up/this), 👇 (point down/wires), 🖐 (5/five? No, I need to ask about the 3 wires). Let's just point to the wires (👇) and then spread hands (👐) to mean "show me" or "what is this?". Or better, point to each wire position if possible, but I'm blind. I'll just point to the general area (👇) and then make a "question" shape or just wait for them to describe.

Let's refine the speech to Mute. It needs to be clear. "Mute, please tell me the defusal rule for the three wires."
Let's refine the gesture to Deaf. "Deaf, what are the colors of wires 1, 2, and 3?"
Gestures: 👇 (wires), ☝ (1), ✌ (2), 🤟 (3 - sign for love/ILY often used for 3 in some contexts, or just 🤘? No, let's use standard counting if possible. In many ASL-inspired sets, 3 is 🤟 or middle/ring/pinky extended. Let's assume Deaf understands basic pointing. I will point to the wire area, then hold up 1, 2, 3 fingers sequentially? That's complex.
Simpler: Point to wires (👇), then open hands (👐) meaning "tell me details".

Let's try to coordinate. If I ask Mute for the rule, and Deaf for the colors, I can combine them.

Message 1 (to Mute): "What is the rule for cutting the wires?"
Message 2 (to Deaf): Gesture: 👇 (indicate wires), 🖐 (stop/wait? no), 👏 (clap? attention). Let's use 👉 (look here) -> 👇 (wires) -> 🤞 (cross fingers/hope? no).
Standard puzzle gesture for "Color": Often not standardized.
Maybe I should just say "Wait" to ensure they process my request? No, I need info.

Let's assume the Deaf monkey knows the wire positions are 1, 2, 3 because they see the board too? The prompt says "You each hold a different piece... You are shown your own share". The Deaf sees the bomb. They likely see the wires labeled 1, 2, 3 or just three wires.

I will send:
1. Speech to Mute: "State the defusal rule for the wires."
2. Gesture to Deaf: 👇 (wires), ☝ (one), ✌ (two), 🤟 (three). This asks "Tell me about wires 1, 2, 3".

```
speak(to="mute", text="State the defusal rule for the wires.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👇", "☝", "✌", "🤟"])
wait()
```

The Deaf monkey has provided the visual state: Display is 8, Light is Green, and Wires are Red, Yellow, Blue (positions 1, 2, 3 respectively). I still lack the defusal rules from the Mute monkey. I have received the visual information from Deaf: Display is 8, Light is Green, and Wires are Red (1), Yellow (2), Blue (3). I also received a direct instruction from Deaf to "CUT THE LEFT WIRE". However, in bomb defusal puzzles, instructions often depend on specific conditions found in the manual. The Mute monkey holds the manual but has not yet provided any rules or confirmed if this instruction is safe given the current state (Display 8, Light Green). Cutting blindly based only on one monkey's observation without cross-referencing the rulebook held by the other is extremely risky. I need to confirm with Mute whether cutting the left wire (Red) is correct for a display of 8 and a green light. If Mute confirms, I will cut. If Mute contradicts or provides different rules, I must follow those. Since I cannot speak to Deaf directly (only gesture, and they just gave an instruction), my priority is to get the rule verification from Mute.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf says cut left wire. Visuals: Disp 8, Light Green, Wires R/Y/B. Confirm if this matches manual rules.")
wait()
```

I must wait for the Mute to provide the actual rule. If the rule says "If display is even, cut red", then Deaf's instruction aligns. If the rule says "If light is green, cut blue", Deaf is wrong. I cannot act until I have the logic from the Manual holder.
